Materialize a patient subgroup as new Postgres schemas

Source: R/access_subcohort.R
materialize_subcohort.Rd

Creates independent schemas (e.g. mimic_iv_demo_cervical_coh, mimic_iv_demo_cervical_coh_concepts, etc.) by filtering all tables from the source schemas to the provided patient IDs. Tables that have no patient ID column (lookup / reference tables) are copied as-is.

Usage

materialize_subcohort(
  src_name,
  ids,
  subgroup_name,
  schemas = c("raw", "concepts", "harmonized"),
  overwrite = FALSE,
  con = NULL
)

Arguments

src_name

Original source name (e.g. "mimic_iv_demo").

ids

Vector of patient IDs from build_subcohort() or custom.

subgroup_name

Short label appended to src_name to form the new source name: {src_name}_{subgroup_name}. Example: "cervical" -> new source "mimic_iv_demo_cervical".

schemas

Which schemas to copy. Default c("raw", "concepts", "harmonized"). Any of: "raw", "concepts", "harmonized", "derived".

overwrite

Drop existing subgroup schemas before recreating. Default FALSE.

con

Optional explicit DBI connection.

Value

Invisibly returns the new source name.

Details

After materialization the subgroup behaves like a regular source: fetch_concept("mimic_iv_demo_cervical", "heart_rate") works without any active-cohort filter.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
ehr_connect("rendehr", creds)

ids <- build_subcohort("mimic_iv_demo", scid_injury_level = "thoracic")

materialize_subcohort("mimic_iv_demo", ids, "thoracic")

# The subgroup is now a first-class source
fetch_concept("mimic_iv_demo_thoracic", "heart_rate")
cohort_summary("mimic_iv_demo_thoracic")

# Clean up when done
drop_subcohort("mimic_iv_demo", "cervical_complete")
} # }
